 Blue Angels' Saturday homecoming air show is the last of the year 
 By Brandon Girod and Benjamin Johnson, Pensacola News Journal 
 USA Today Network via Reuters Connect 
 Updated November 7, 2026 5:21 AM 
 The Blue Angels soar over NAS Pensacola during the homecoming air show on Nov. 6, 2026.
 Tony Giberson
 USA TODAY Network, Reuters 
 The Blue Angels 2026 Homecoming Air Show on Saturday will be the team's last performance of the year. 
 Scheduled for Nov. 6 and 7, the Blue Angels Homecoming Air Show takes place onboard NAS Pensacola and serves as the team's final show before it begins winter training.
 This year's show is a special one because the team was forced to cancel last year's homecoming show due to the U.S. government shutdown, which restricted access to NAS Pensacola. 
 Here's everything you need to know about the 2026 Pensacola Blue Angels Homecoming Air Show.
 Where is the Blue Angels No. 6 jet?
 Maj. Scott Laux, the opposing solo flying jet No. 6 and second-year member of the Blue Angels, was removed from the flight demonstration squadron and will not perform in the homecoming air show celebrating NAS Pensacola's 200-year anniversary, Chief of Naval Air Training (CNATRA) confirmed to the News Journal Nov. 6.
 "Blue Angel #6 was removed from the team for failing to uphold the standards expected of members of the Navy Flight Demonstration Squadron and will not participate in the team's remaining performance this season," CNATRA's public affairs office said in an emailed statement.
 The team flew five jets instead of the standard six during the NAS Pensacola Homecoming Air show on Friday. 
 When is the 2026 Blue Angels Homecoming Air Show?
 Both the Main Gate, at the south end of Navy Boulevard, and the West Gate, at the south end of Blue Angel Parkway, will open at 8 a.m. both days. The air show is scheduled to start at 9:30 a.m.
 When will the Blue Angels fly?
 The Blue Angels are scheduled to fly around 2 p.m. Assuming everything goes according to schedule, fans can expect to see them perform between 2 and 2:45 p.m. Fat Albert typically flies for about 15 minutes before the Blue Angels, but is grounded for maintenance until 2027.
 What time should you head to the Blue Angels Homecoming Air Show?
 You should plan to arrive around 8 a.m., which is when gates will open. Patrons who arrive earlier could be turned away at the gate. 
 Who is performing at the 2026 Blue Angels Homecoming Air Show?
 The Blue Angels serve as the headliner to the air show each year. Here's who else is scheduled to perform ahead of the Blue Angels, according to official air show information.
 Stearman Flight Team
 Rusty "Crash" Miller
 Daniel "Doc" Serrato
 Tanner Matheny
 Jeff Shetterly
 Redline Airshows
 Adam Baker Airshows
 Ghostwriter
 Tom Larkin – Minijet
 Brian Correll Airshows
 Precision Exotics
 Mike Goulian
 Rad Aerosports
 Socomm para-commandos
 F-35C Lightning II
 U.S. Air Force F-16 Viper
 U.S. Blue Angels
 Do I need an ID to see the Blue Angels Homecoming Air Show?
 Yes. All individuals 18 and older must have a valid REAL ID to access NAS Pensacola for the air show.
 Passports can be used in lieu of an ID. Passports are mandatory for foreign nationals.
 Non-U.S. citizens are also allowed to attend the air show, but will need a valid passport and may be subject to additional screening requirements, according to the U.S. Navy.
 Do I need to buy a ticket for the Blue Angels Homecoming Air Show?
 No. The Blue Angels Homecoming Air Show is free to the public. Premium seating for the air show is sold out.
 What should you bring to a Blue Angels air show?
 The Blue Angels Homecoming Air Show isn't quite the all-day affair that the Pensacola Beach air show is, but it's close. Here are some things you should consider bringing to maximize your enjoyment.
 Hearing protection: Everyone should have some sort of hearing protection because the Blue Angels' F/A-18 Super Hornets are loud, with noise levels sometimes exceeding 100 decibels.
 Comfortable clothing and footwear: With gates opening at 8 a.m. and the Blue Angels flying around 2 p.m., it's a good idea to wear clothing and shoes you'll feel comfortable in for several hours. Average temperatures are expected to be around the mid-70s, but consider bringing a light jacket or sweater as the tarmac can get windy.
 Hats, sunscreen and sunglasses: The general admission area will be shadeless, and umbrellas are discouraged, so the team recommends bringing hats and sunglasses. Don't forget to grab some sunscreen and to reapply every couple of hours.
 Foldable chairs and a blanket: Foldable chairs and blankets are encouraged, especially in the general admission area. Just note that umbrellas are discouraged as they block the view of other patrons.
 Strollers and wheelchairs: There are no vendors that offer stroller or wheelchair rentals, so patrons are encouraged to bring their own, if needed.
 Small purses, diaper bags and small camera bags: Only small purses, diaper bags and small camera bags are allowed, so make sure you only pack what can fit in these bags or that you can carry by hand.
 Here's a list of other permitted items:
 Cellphones, laptops and tablets
 FRS/GMRS radios and VHF band and other scanners (transmitters/receivers are not allowed)
 Photography and camera equipment (must be carried in a small camera bag or by hand)
 Coolers, outside food and beverages and pets not allowed
 The Blue Angels Homecoming Air Show prohibits the following:
 Coolers
 Drones
 Pets
 Outside food and beverages
 Pop-up tents
 Weapons
 Drugs
 Most bags (except small purses and diaper bags)
 Roller skates, skateboards, bikes or personal golf carts
 Where do I park for the Blue Angels Homecoming Air Show?
 Motorists will be directed to the nearest available parking areas by security personnel. As parking fills, security will direct motorists to parking lots that have shuttle service to and from the air show. General admission parking is free.
